Report specs and pages

Source: R/report_spec.R
pub_report_spec.Rd

A report spec describes how a document becomes a report in one format: templates, front matter, table of contents, page, figures, caption labels and more.

Usage

pub_report_spec(
  format = c("html", "docx", "pdf", "md"),
  reference_docx = NULL,
  latex_preamble = NULL,
  typst_template = NULL,
  front_matter = NULL,
  toc = TRUE,
  toc_depth = 3L,
  number_sections = TRUE,
  labels = list(table = "Table", figure = "Figure"),
  page = NULL,
  figure = NULL,
  placeholder_color = NULL,
  lock = NULL,
  error_items = c("refuse", "show"),
  post_process = list(),
  pandoc_args = character()
)

pub_page(
  size = c("a4", "letter"),
  orientation = c("portrait", "landscape"),
  margins = NULL
)

Arguments

format

Output format: "html", "docx", "pdf" or "md".

reference_docx

Path of the reference document of DOCX reports, or NULL (pubflow's).

latex_preamble

Path of a LaTeX file included in the preamble of PDF reports made with xelatex, or NULL.

typst_template

Path of the pandoc template of PDF reports made with Typst, or NULL (pubflow's).

front_matter

function(doc, format) returning the front matter, or NULL (the title block: title, subtitle, author and time; shown only with a title, subtitle or author).

toc

TRUE: add a table of contents (see Details).

toc_depth

integer(1) deepest heading level in it (1-6).

number_sections

TRUE: number the sections.

labels

Named list of the caption words table and figure.

page

A pub_page() or NULL.

figure

Device settings of figures (see Details) or NULL.

placeholder_color

Colour of placeholders ("#rrggbb") or NULL.

lock

TRUE, FALSE or NULL (see Details).

error_items

"refuse" or "show".

post_process

List of post-processors (see Details).

pandoc_args

character extra arguments of pandoc.

size

Paper size: "a4" or "letter".

orientation

"portrait" or "landscape".

margins

Named numeric margins in cm (top, bottom, left, right; missing ones are 2.5, at the bottom 2), or NULL.

Value

A pub_report_spec or pub_page object.

Details

Functions

  • pub_report_spec() creates a spec. Pass it as spec to pub_render() or pub_markdown().

  • pub_page() describes the page (size, orientation, margins) of DOCX and PDF reports.

All arguments except format and error_items are optional: NULL means the default (for figure and labels, an empty list does too).

Which argument acts where

Every argument acts in every format that can show it. Setting an argument that the format can't use is an error, e.g. placeholder_color for DOCX, where the reference document's "Placeholder" style sets the colour.

Variants of a spec

To make variants (e.g. one per report and format, sharing the front matter), call pub_report_spec() again, e.g. from a helper function of your app. A value that you edit afterwards (spec$toc <- FALSE) is checked only when the spec is used.

The arguments in detail

  • front_matter: a function(doc, format) that returns the front matter, e.g. a title page with a signature table. It replaces the title block (in HTML the header) in every format; the title and author stay in the file's properties.

    • It returns what a document can hold: sections, outputs or lists of them (see pub_doc()).

    • doc is the document with the render-time metadata (see pub_render()) and format the output format.

    • Its sections are unnumbered (the numbers of the body start at 1), while its tables and figures count in the caption numbers.

    • End it with pub_pagebreak() to start the table of contents on a new page.

  • toc: TRUE adds a table of contents of the headings up to level toc_depth after the front matter (or title block).

    • It is left out if the document has no sections, or if the document or the front matter places a pub_toc() itself.

    • Word fills it in when its fields are updated.

    • For lists of figures and tables, place pub_toc(what = "figures") or pub_toc(what = "tables"), e.g. in the front matter.

  • number_sections: FALSE leaves every heading unnumbered (in Word the "Heading n Unnumbered" styles).

  • labels: the words before the caption numbers, list(table, figure).

  • page: a pub_page().

    • By default, DOCX keeps the page of the reference document and PDF is A4 portrait with margins of 2.5 cm (2 cm at the bottom).

    • An explicit page applies to every section of a DOCX file.

    • A landscape page turns the whole document, so landscape sections and items in it stay on the same pages.

  • figure: list(device, res), the image format and the resolution of PNG images in dpi. It is merged over the default: PNG with 200 dpi, as in the viewer, so a report after viewing reuses the cached figures and shows them as the viewer did. "svg" (HTML, Markdown and PDF via Typst) and "pdf" (PDF via LaTeX) give vector images.

  • placeholder_color: colour of [text]{.placeholder} spans, e.g. "#0083c0" (the default of PDF; HTML uses #0077b0 for better contrast).

  • lock: DOCX only. TRUE locks the header, the footer and every table and figure that isn't pub_set_meta(locked = FALSE) against accidental editing and deletion (see pub_pp_docx_lock()). NULL (default) locks only the tables and figures with pub_set_meta(locked = TRUE), and the header and footer if post_process lists pub_pp_docx_lock(). FALSE locks nothing, and post_process can't list pub_pp_docx_lock().

  • error_items: what pub_render() does with error items (failed steps placed by a layout step run with on_error = "continue", see pub_doc()):

    • "refuse" (default) signals a pubflow_render_error;

    • "show" writes their error boxes and warns (pubflow_render_warning), naming the failed steps.

  • post_process: a list of functions function(path, doc, spec) that change the rendered file before it is copied to its destination.

    • They are called in order. path is the file, doc the document with the render-time metadata and spec this spec.

    • They change the file in place; their value is ignored. A failing one is a pubflow_render_error and no file is written.

    • DOCX reports first get pub_pp_docx_header_footer() and (with lock) pub_pp_docx_lock(). List one of them to give it arguments or another place.

    • pub_pp_docx_header_footer() and pub_pp_docx_lock() can't be used for other formats.

  • pandoc_args: pandoc options added after pubflow's (so they override them), one argument per element.

Custom templates

Start from pubflow's template and keep what pubflow writes into it:

  • reference_docx (start from system.file("templates", "reference.docx", package = "pubflow")):

    • paragraph styles "Heading 1"-"Heading 5", "Heading 1 Unnumbered"-"Heading 5 Unnumbered", "Item Title", "Table Caption", "Image Caption", "Figure" and "Error", and the character style "Placeholder" (missing styles are added unformatted);

    • for header and footer lines, the bookmarks header_left, header_center, header_right, footer_left, footer_center and footer_right in its header and footer (only those of the lines you use, see pub_pp_docx_header_footer()).

  • latex_preamble: a file included after pubflow's header (which loads the packages for tables, landscape pages, header and footer, and the frame of error items) and before the document's header and footer lines.

  • typst_template (start from system.file("templates", "pubflow.typ", package = "pubflow")): a pandoc template that

    • writes $header-includes$ (page orientation and caption labels);

    • shows the title block only if $title-block$ is set;

    • takes the header and footer lines from $header-left$ to $footer-right$ (an empty part also sets $footer-right-empty$ etc.).

See also

pub_render(), pub_trace_stamp(), pub_pp_docx_header_footer()

Examples

# A spec for one format; printing it shows what it uses
spec <- pub_report_spec(
    "pdf",
    page = pub_page("letter", margins = c(left = 3)),
    labels = list(table = "Tab.", figure = "Fig."),
    front_matter = function(doc, format) {
        list(pub_text(paste("Prepared by", doc$meta$author)),
             pub_pagebreak())
    }
)
spec
#> <pubflow report spec: pdf>
#>   latex_preamble    none
#>   typst_template    default
#>   front_matter      function
#>   toc               depth 3
#>   number_sections   yes
#>   page              Letter portrait, margins top 2.5, bottom 2, left 3, right 2.5 cm
#>   figure            default
#>   labels            Tab., Fig.
#>   placeholder_color default
#>   error_items       refuse
#>   post_process      none
#>   pandoc_args       none
pub_report_spec("docx", toc = FALSE, error_items = "show")
#> <pubflow report spec: docx>
#>   reference_docx    default
#>   front_matter      title block
#>   toc               no
#>   number_sections   yes
#>   page              reference document
#>   figure            default
#>   labels            Table, Figure
#>   lock              marked items
#>   error_items       show
#>   post_process      none
#>   pandoc_args       none

# Landscape page and vector figures
pub_report_spec("pdf", page = pub_page("a4", "landscape"),
                figure = list(device = "pdf"))
#> <pubflow report spec: pdf>
#>   latex_preamble    none
#>   typst_template    default
#>   front_matter      title block
#>   toc               depth 3
#>   number_sections   yes
#>   page              A4 landscape, margins top 2.5, bottom 2, left 2.5, right 2.5 cm
#>   figure            device = pdf
#>   labels            Table, Figure
#>   placeholder_color default
#>   error_items       refuse
#>   post_process      none
#>   pandoc_args       none

# Use a spec to render (HTML needs nothing but pubflow)
doc <- pub_doc(
    pub_section("Results", pub_text("All batches meet the limits.")),
    meta = list(title = "Demo report", author = "Jane Doe")
)
html <- pub_report_spec("html", toc = FALSE, number_sections = FALSE)
path <- pub_render(doc, "html", file = tempfile(fileext = ".html"), spec = html)

# A post-processor changes the finished file, here by appending a comment
add_note <- function(path, doc, spec) {
    writeLines(c(readLines(path), "<!-- checked -->"), path)
}
html <- pub_report_spec("html", post_process = add_note)
path <- pub_render(doc, "html", file = tempfile(fileext = ".html"), spec = html)
tail(readLines(path), 1)
#> [1] "<!-- checked -->"

# Variants: one spec per format that share the front matter and the labels
title_page <- function(doc, format) {
    list(pub_text(paste("Prepared by", doc$meta$author)), pub_pagebreak())
}
my_report_spec <- function(format) {
    pub_report_spec(
        format,
        front_matter = title_page,
        labels = list(table = "Tab.", figure = "Fig.")
    )
}
my_report_spec("docx")
#> <pubflow report spec: docx>
#>   reference_docx    default
#>   front_matter      function
#>   toc               depth 3
#>   number_sections   yes
#>   page              reference document
#>   figure            default
#>   labels            Tab., Fig.
#>   lock              marked items
#>   error_items       refuse
#>   post_process      none
#>   pandoc_args       none
my_report_spec("md")
#> <pubflow report spec: md>
#>   front_matter      function
#>   toc               no
#>   number_sections   yes
#>   figure            default
#>   labels            Tab., Fig.
#>   error_items       refuse
#>   post_process      none

# An argument that the format can't use is refused
try(pub_report_spec("docx", placeholder_color = "#0083c0"))
#> Error in pub_report_spec("docx", placeholder_color = "#0083c0") : 
#>   `placeholder_color` can't be used for docx reports, only for html and pdf.
